questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the secretory or exocytotic pathway of protein sorting?

options.label: A
options.text: Endoplasmic Reticulum→ Golgi Apparatus→ Plasma Membrane→ Release into the external environment

options.label: B
options.text: Golgi Apparatus→ Endoplasmic Reticulum→ Plasma Membrane→ Release into the external environment

options.label: C
options.text: Plasma Membrane→ Endoplasmic Reticulum→ Golgi Apparatus→ Release into the external environment

options.label: D
options.text: Plasma Membrane→ Golgi Apparatus → Endoplasmic Reticulum →Release into the external environment

questions.answerText: Endoplasmic Reticulum→ Golgi Apparatus→ Plasma Membrane→ Release into the external environment
questions.solutionHtml:
Endoplasmic Reticulum→ Golgi Apparatus→ Plasma Membrane→ Release into the external environment
  • In the secretory or exocytotic pathway, proteins are transported from the Endoplasmic Reticulum → Golgi Apparatus → Plasma Membrane and then released into the external environment. This is done through the formation of secretory vesicles.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 583

questions.stem: In order to keep ion gradients across their membrane, red blood cells need ATP in the absence of which they will enlarge and burst causing hemolytic anemia. The main process by which RBCs generate their energy is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Substrate-level phosphorylation
  • Red blood cells do not contain mitochondria and can only generate energy via anaerobic glycolysis with the production of lactate and production of ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 655

questions.stem: Lipids present in Inner Mitochondrial Membrane (IMM) assist in the proper activity of proteins and enzyme complexes of ETC. A major lipid present in IMM is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cardiolipin
  • Cardiolipin is a phospholipid that is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane
  • It is found only in mitochondria
  • It has a complex structure made up of glycerol attached to two Phosphatidic acids.

Properties and Function

  • It has a role in apoptosis signaling
  • It acts as an anticoagulant
  • It increases the efficiency of oxidative phosphorylation by acting as a proton trap.

Barth Syndrome – a rare X-linked disorder, that occurs due to defects in cardiolipin remodeling. Patients have muscle weakness, neutropenia, and cardiomyopathy




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 211

questions.stem: A variety of dietary plans and exercise regimen are recommended and used by dietitians and trainers for weight management. One of them among is Atkins diet which is a:
questions.solutionHtml:
Low calorie, low carbohydrate diet
  • Atkin’s diet is a weight-loss diet that is low in calorie and also low in carbohydrates. It was originally promoted by the physician Dr. Robert C. Atkins.
  • For weight reduction, the amount of carbohydrates taken in the diet should be less as carbohydrate gets converted to fats in the body, which is called endogenous fat and it gets transported in the form of VLDL



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 190

questions.stem: High-energy phosphate compound is/are:ATPCreatine phosphateGlucose- 1- phosphateGlycerol -3-phosphateADPSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1, 2, and 5 are correct

Statement 1 and 5: ATP and ADP

  • The high-energy compounds are those which release standard free energy on their hydrolysis which is generally coupled for the formation of ATP or other precursors used in synthesis or catabolic reactions.
  • Energy is released because products formed after hydrolysis are in more stable forms than the original compound.
  • The hydrolysis of anhydride P-O bonds are exergonic and releases energy with large negative ΔGo.

Statement: 2: Creatine Phosphate

  • Creatine phosphate aka phosphocreatine is a phosphorylated creatine molecule.
  • It serves as a rapidly mobilizable source of energy in skeletal muscle, myocardium, and the brain.
  • It helps in the formation of ATP from ADP by coupling its hydrolysis to creatine and phosphate.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 111-112

options.label: C

questions.answerText: A- T, B- T, C- F, D- T, E- T
questions.solutionHtml:
A- T, B- T, C- F, D- T, E- T

Statement A: Increased number and size of lysosomes

  • Lysosomal storage disorders are inborn diseases due to the lack or inactivity of lysosomal hydrolases, transporters, or integral membrane proteins.
  • In order to make up for the loss of activity there is induction of lysosome biogenesis (increase in lysosome number).
  • Substrate accumulation in lysosomes increases the size of lysosomes

questions.stem: Mitochondria are involved in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cholesterol synthesis

Cholesterol synthesis

  • It is an anabolic pathway and anabolic pathways generally occur in the cytoplasm.
  • Most of the steps of cholesterol synthesis also occur in cytoplasm however last few steps (after squalene synthesis) occur in ER.
  • Insulin activates this pathway by promoting dephosphorylation of RLE HMG CoA reductase.


Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 260

questions.stem: Proteins are produced by the process of translation, is directed by messenger RNA (mRNA). Which of the following cellular component is directly involved in the process of protein synthesis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ribosomes
  • The main process of protein synthesis occurs in ribosomes.
  • Ribosomes are made of two subunits that come together at the start of translation.
  • mRNA gets bound by ribosomal protein synthetic machinery to give rise to native polypeptides.


Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No 415

questions.stem: Which of the following is not the source of cytosolic NADPH?
questions.solutionHtml:
ATP citrate lyase
  • It is an enzyme involved in citrate shuttle that is used to supply substrates for fatty acid synthesis.
  • It converts citrate to oxaloacetate and acetyl CoA using CoA and ATP (Generally, Lyases do not use ATP)
  • It is an anabolic enzyme but active in the phosphorylated state as an exception. Generally, anabolic enzymes are active in a dephosphorylated state.

Sources of cytosolic NADPH



Satyanarayana Biochemistry 4th Edition Page No. 274

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a major function of the endoplasmic reticulum?

options.label: C
options.text: Providing enzymes that control glycogen breakdown

options.label: D
options.text: Secretion of proteins synthesized in the cell

questions.answerText: Secretion of proteins synthesized in the cell
questions.solutionHtml:
Secretion of proteins synthesized in the cell
  • Though folding and some post-translational modifications of newly synthesized proteins are done in ER, packaging and secretion of proteins is mainly done by the Golgi apparatus.
  • In the secretory or exocytotic pathway, proteins are transported from the Endoplasmic Reticulum → Golgi Apparatus → Plasma Membrane and then released into the external environment. This is done through secretory vesicles.




Dinesh Puri Textbook of Biochemistry 3rd Edition Page No -131

questions.stem: A child presents with hypotonia and seizures. It was confirmed to be Zellweger syndrome. Which of the following accumulates in the brain?
questions.solutionHtml:
Long-chain fatty acid

Zellweger syndrome

  • It is also called as Cerebro-Hepato-Renal Syndrome.
  • It is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder.
  • Absence of Peroxisomes in almost all tissues, peroxisomes are responsible for the oxidation of very long chain fatty acids (VLCFA) which contain more than 22 carbons. So, accumulation of VLCFA (C > 22) occurs especially in the brain, as brain sphingomyelins are rich in long-chain fatty acids.

Clinical features:

  • Severe neurological symptoms such as Impaired neuronal migration, hypomyelination, hepatomegaly, and renal cysts.
  • Most patients die within 1st year of their life.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No 224

questions.stem: Intercellular communication in Eukaryotes is mediated by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Exosomes
  • Exosomes are extracellular vesicles that contain constituents (protein, DNA, RNA) of the cells that secrete them.
  • They are taken up by distant cells which can affect cell function and behavior.
  • So, they are involved in intercellular communication through the exchange of material and information between cells.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No 483

questions.stem: Which of the following food is having a high thermic effect?
questions.solutionHtml:
Proteins
  • Specific dynamic action (SDA), also known as the thermic effect of food (TEF) is the amount of energy expenditure above the basal metabolic rate due to the cost of processing food for use and storage.
  • As it refers to the heat produced after eating it is known as dietary-induced thermogenesis (DIT)
  • For example, dietary fat is very easy to process and has very little thermic effect, while protein is hard to process and has a much larger thermic effect.
  • High SDA of proteins is generally attributed to meeting the energy requirements for oxidative deamination, synthesis of urea, and biosynthesis of proteins.
